corrections: reader_sound BLOCKER #1 — section-symbol-relative relocs. Verified: the linker resolve loop (elf_x86_64.hexa:1015-1029) resolves EVERY reloc BY NAME (reads sym.name_offset -> name, linear-searches def_names). This works only because pack_lir_x86_64 emits relocs exclusively against NAMED symbols (.LCstrN/g<id>, confirmed @1515-1577). A clang-compiled runtime_core.o instead emits R_X86_64_PC32/PLT32/64 relocs against STT_SECTION symbols (st_name=0 -> name='', st_value=0, addend=offset-into-section) for local string/static-table/jump-table references — pervasive in a C runtime. The design's parse plan copies the empty name and does nothing special, so at link time all section symbols collapse to name '' : first-match resolves to the WRONG section, or found_idx=-1 -> reloc SILENTLY SKIPPED (@1030 guard) = miscompile. This is exactly the 'reloc-resolve loop assumes something pack_lir sets that a parsed member won't' failure. FIX: reader must synthesize a UNIQUE name per STT_SECTION symbol (e.g. \"$sec<memberIdx>_<shndx>\") pushed into obj.strtab AND register it as a def with value=that section's concat pool base; OR switch the resolve loop to (obj,index)-keyed resolution for parsed members instead of name-keyed. Without one of these, round-3 cannot correctly link runtime_core.o.

reader_sound BLOCKER #2 — multiple/function-section .text. The design concatenates .rodata.*/.data.* but treats obj.text as a single slice of the section literally named '.text', mapping 'everything else non-alloc -> 0'. If runtime.a members are built with -ffunction-sections (or merely carry .text.unlikely/.text.hot/.init), those sections are ALLOC+EXECINSTR yet fall into the 'else -> 0' bucket and their bytes (whole function bodies) are DROPPED. FIX: treat .text and .text.* symmetrically to the rodata/data pools — concat into obj.text with a per-source-section base, and rebase BOTH symbol st_value AND reloc r_offset for text-resident symbols/relocs into the concatenated text-pool offset (the plan only rebases rodata/data). Confirm the actual runtime.a build flags on the pool before sizing this.

reader_sound gap #3 (lower severity) — COMMON symbols. Design maps SHN_COMMON -> 'bss marker' but never allocates per-COMMON bss space nor assigns distinct offsets. For a COMMON sym st_value is the ALIGNMENT and st_size the byte size; multiple COMMONs would all resolve to bss offset 0. Modern clang defaults -fno-common (clang>=11) so tentative defs normally land in .bss, making this rare — but if present it silently aliases. FIX: per COMMON sym, round bss_size up to st_value alignment, set the sym value to the new offset, then bss_size += st_size.

testable_incrementally caveat — the Stage-1 serialize->parse round-trip is hermetic and genuinely stage-separable (staging is NOT big-bang, so the flag stays true), BUT it exercises the reader ONLY against hexa's OWN writer output, which by construction contains none of the clang patterns behind gaps #1-#3 (no section-symbol relocs, single .text, no COMMON). The round-trip test will pass GREEN while the reader is still broken for real members — false confidence. ADD: a committed tiny real clang -c x86_64-linux .o fixture (string literal + static table, checked in as a byte array) to the Stage-1 unit test so section-symbol relocs + multi-section layout are exercised HERMETICALLY before the pool-only Stage 4. Otherwise the reader-vs-clang soundness is effectively first-tested at Stage 4.

boundary/test-symbol caveat (method right, example under-validated) — the two-tier boundary (3a libc-free minimal exec as the gate, 3b sanctioned-libc-floor as the named wall) is correct and matches the repo's sanctioned-floor doctrine. But the concrete example `hexa_add(40,2)` is NOT verified libc-free: HexaVal arithmetic/boxing may transitively pull hexa_box/alloc -> mmap-arena malloc, so its closure may still need alloc_syscall_native.o (or hit libc). The test_plan's own method (dump the transitive member+UND closure on the pool, pick the fewest-member libc-free leaf) is the right gate — just don't presume hexa_add qualifies; be prepared that the smallest runnable 3a symbol may have to INCLUDE alloc_syscall_native.o, or the milestone slips to a pure non-boxing leaf.

byteeq note (safe, guard the invariant) — round-1/2 stay byte-identical because exit_code/hello_str are UND-free (literal exit; inline-write string), so the UND-gated dispatch keeps them on the plain link_elf_x86_64_ownstart, and even if rerouted, extracted=[] makes all_objs==program_objs. Two invariants to actually assert in the byteeq 3-target run: (a) the _ar wrapper with extracted=[] emits bytes identical to the plain fn (holds by construction — same loop), and (b) edit-B's new data-site reloc branch never fires for pack_lir objs — its ElfRel site-segment tag MUST default to text so a member-free build is unperturbed.

These parse on-disk ELF .o bytes today (just return [int] offsets, not an ElfX86Obj) — parse_elf_x86_obj = compose these idioms into an ElfX86Obj builder. The ownstart linker's def/reloc resolve loop (compiler/emit/elf_x86_64.hexa:920-1065) already consumes ElfX86Obj[] and resolves PC32/PLT32/64 across objs with section-slot convention {1=.text, 3=.rodata, >=4=.data} and first-match symbol precedence — extraction feeds directly into it by growing objs[]; MUST-WRITE-NEW is only the data-segment patch-site branch (:1041-1060 today text-only, comment @1042-1043 explicitly defers data->data to round-3).

The writer serialize_elf_x86_64 (:1080-1325) is the exact byte layout the reader inverts (STN_UNDEF idx-0 prepend, r_info sym+1 shift, LOCAL<GLOBAL sh_info=nlocal+1, section order NULL/.text/.rela.text/.rodata/.data/.bss/.symtab/.strtab/.shstrtab) — reverse-engineer the reader against it AND use serialize->parse round-trip as the hermetic unit test.
read_file_bytes(path) is an available builtin (used throughout hexa_ld.hexa :1480,:2737...) — the byte slurp for both runtime.a and the .o reader; write_bytes already used by the linker.

pack_lir_x86_64 UND-emit convention (:1932-1946, section=0 SHN_UNDEF bind=GLOBAL) and _find_elf_sym_by_name (:2046) show how UND vs def symbols are represented — the fixpoint's live-UND detection keys off section==0.

main.hexa integration seam already exists: elf_obj_x86_holder:[ElfX86Obj] (:837), pushed at :1085, passed to link_elf_x86_64_ownstart at :1248 under linker_kind=='hexa' — swap to the _ar wrapper when the program carries runtime UNDs.

components.name: parse_ar_archive (GNU ar reader)
components.plan: Input = read_file_bytes(runtime.a) -> [Int] `buf`. Verify magic: bytes[0..8] == '!<arch>\n' (21 3c 61 72 63 68 3e 0a) else return []. Then walk 60-byte member headers starting at off=8: name = buf[hdr+0 .. hdr+16] (16B ASCII), size = decimal-ASCII parse of buf[hdr+48 .. hdr+58], header magic buf[hdr+58..60] must be 0x60 0x0a ('`\n'). Member DATA begins at hdr+60, length=size; advance off = hdr+60+size, then 2-byte even-pad (if off odd, off+=1). SPECIAL MEMBERS: name starting '/ '(0x2f 0x20) or '/ '==armap/symbol-index -> SKIP (do not add). name '// ' -> the long-name string table; capture its [data_off,size] as `longnames`. A NORMAL name is slash-terminated GNU form 'foo.o/' -> strip at first '/'; a name of form '/<decimal>' -> index into longnames: read a NUL/newline-terminated cstr at longnames.data_off+decimal. Emit one ArMember per real .o member. Return [ArMember] where struct ArMember { name: string, data_off: Int, size: Int } references the master buf (no byte copy). Reuse the writer module's byte idiom; add a private decimal-ASCII helper `_ar_dec(buf, off, n)`. NOTE: the darwin-local runtime.a is BSD ar (#1/N ext-names + __.SYMDEF, Mach-O members) — NOT the target; round-3 targets the pool linux GNU-ar/ELF archive, so BSD-ar handling is out of scope (documented caveat for the darwin unit test, which hand-builds GNU-ar bytes).

components.name: parse_elf_x86_obj (on-disk ELF64 REL -> ElfX86Obj)
components.plan: Input = a member byte-slice base+size within `buf` (pass buf + base + limit; all reads offset by base). Guard is_elf64_le at base and e_type(base+0x10)==ET_REL(1), e_machine(base+0x12)==EM_X86_64(0x3e). Read section-header table: e_shoff=u64(base+0x28), e_shentsize=u16(base+0x3A), e_shnum=u16(base+0x3C), e_shstrndx=u16(base+0x3E); shstr_off = u64(sh(e_shstrndx)+0x18). Walk e_shnum section headers (each 64B; fields sh_name@0x00 u32, sh_type@0x04 u32, sh_flags@0x08, sh_offset@0x18 u64, sh_size@0x20 u64, sh_link@0x28 u32, sh_info@0x2C u32, sh_entsize@0x38 u64) EXACTLY like hexa_ld find_sections/find_rela_text. First pass: record, per section index, its name + [file_off,size,type] and build a section-index -> NORMALIZED-slot map: the section named '.text' -> slot 1; '.rodata'(and .rodata.*/.rodata.cst*) -> slot 3; '.data'(and .data.*) -> slot 4; '.bss'(SHT_NOBITS) -> a bss marker; everything else non-alloc -> 0. Copy raw bytes: obj.text = slice(.text), obj.rodata = concat of rodata sections, obj.data = concat of data sections, obj.bss_size += each SHT_NOBITS sh_size; remember per-source-section the byte base within obj.rodata/obj.data so symbol st_value (section-relative) can be rebased into the concatenated pool offset. Second pass SHT_SYMTAB (24B entries: st_name@0x00 u32, st_info@0x04 u8 [bind=info>>4,type=info&0xf], st_shndx@0x06 u16, st_value@0x08 u64, st_size@0x10 u64): for each symbol build ElfSym{ name_offset, section, value, size, bind, type_ } where name is copied into obj.strtab (new local strtab: push a leading 0 like pack_lir, append each name via _ew_str, name_offset = returned offset) and `section` is the NORMALIZED slot of st_shndx (0 for SHN_UNDEF; 1/3/4 for text/rodata/data; SHN_COMMON->bss; SHN_ABS 0xfff1 -> keep 0/skip-as-def), and `value` is rebased pool offset (st_value + that source-section's concat base). nlocal = count of STB_LOCAL defs. Third pass SHT_RELA sections ('.rela.text','.rela.data',...): for each 24B Elf64_Rela (r_offset@0x00, r_info@0x08 [sym=r_info>>32, type=r_info&0xffffffff], r_addend@0x10 signed) build ElfRel{ offset: r_offset (+ the target-section's concat base when the rela applies to .data/.rodata so the site offset is pool-relative), sym_idx: the r_info high-32 index into THIS member's symtab == index into the obj.symbols[] we just built (1:1 order preserved, minus the STN_UNDEF idx-0 slot -> subtract 1 to match obj.symbols 0-based), kind: type, addend: r_addend }. Reuse the exact offset constants + _read_u8/16/32/64le/_read_cstr idioms proven in hexa_ld.hexa (copy as local _er_* helpers to keep the round-3 code self-contained in elf_x86_64.hexa).
components.signature: pub fn parse_elf_x86_obj(buf: [Int], base: Int, limit: Int) -> ElfX86Obj

components.name: archive_extract_fixpoint (live-UND driven member pull)
components.plan: Inputs: program_objs (the ElfX86Obj[] already in elf_obj_x86_holder) + members (from parse_ar_archive) + buf. Step 1: build the live-UND set = every symbol name with section==0 (SHN_UNDEF) across all program_objs (read name out of each obj.strtab via name_offset), MINUS names already defined by any program obj (section!=0). Step 2: build a member-provides index: for each ArMember, cheaply scan its ELF .symtab for GLOBAL defs (section!=0, bind==GLOBAL) -> list of exported names (do a light symtab-only walk, not a full parse, to keep it cheap). Step 3 fixpoint loop: repeat until no change — for each not-yet-pulled member, if it exports any name currently in the live-UND set, PULL it: full parse_elf_x86_obj -> ElfX86Obj, append to `extracted`, remove its provided names from live-UND, and ADD its own fresh UNDs (section==0 names not yet defined by program+extracted) to live-UND. Iterate (runtime members reference each other: num_core -> hexa_bool/hexa_truthy -> other members). Terminate when a full pass pulls nothing. Return `extracted` (the transitively-needed members, program order preserved). Remaining live-UND after fixpoint = the sanctioned libc floor (see boundary).

components.name: ownstart integration (grow objs[] + data-segment reloc patch + main wire)
components.plan: New pub wrapper: link_elf_x86_64_ownstart_ar(program_objs, out_path, main_name, archive_path). Body: buf=read_file_bytes(archive_path); members=parse_ar_archive(buf); extracted=archive_extract_fixpoint(program_objs, members, buf); build all_objs = program_objs ++ extracted (program FIRST so the resolve loop's first-match linear def_names scan gives program>archive symbol precedence naturally). Then run the EXISTING ownstart body over all_objs. TWO real edits to the existing link_elf_x86_64_ownstart loop (must be byte-neutral for the no-archive round-1/2 path — the new branches never fire there): (A) the def-collection at :948-968 already handles section 1/3/>=4 which the normalized reader emits; no change needed beyond confirming COMMON/bss defs land in a bss slot. (B) EXTEND the reloc-apply loop (:1041-1060) which today ONLY writes into text_bytes[patch_off]: runtime members carry relocs whose PATCH SITE is in .data/.rodata (e.g. a static function-pointer or string-pointer table -> R_X86_64_64 data->{text,data}). Add: if the reloc's owning section is a data/rodata section, compute the target vaddr the same way (text seg vs data seg) and write the 8-byte absolute (or 4-byte PC32) into data_bytes[obj_data_base/obj_rodata_base + site] instead of text_bytes. This requires tracking, per reloc, whether its site is text or data (carry a site-segment tag from parse_elf_x86_obj, or key off whether r.offset falls in the obj's text vs its rodata/data concat range). Confirmed byte-neutral for round-1/2 because those programs emit zero data-resident relocs. Then main.hexa:1248 wire: when elf_obj_x86_ready and the program has any unresolved runtime UND, resolve archive_path = env HEXA_PREBUILT_RUNTIME else default ~/.hx/bin/build/runtime.a, and call link_elf_x86_64_ownstart_ar instead of link_elf_x86_64_ownstart (fall back to the plain fn when the program is runtime-free, preserving round-1/2 byte output).

boundary_decision: Round-3 CANNOT hold the literal round-1/2 gate ('0 UND, self-contained') for ARBITRARY programs, because pulling runtime.a members drags in symbols the members themselves leave UND — and runtime_core's authoritative nm-UND floor is the sanctioned libc set (malloc/free/write/memcpy/memset/__errno_location/mmap...), which archive extraction cannot manufacture. runtime.a does NOT fully self-satisfy its own UNDs; it bottoms out at libc. So the honest round-3 boundary is TWO-TIER: (3a-MILESTONE, the success gate for THIS round) pick a MINIMAL test symbol whose transitive member-closure inside runtime.a is libc-FREE, so the linked ET_EXEC has nm-UND == ∅ and runs with ZERO binutils AND zero libc — this preserves the round-1/2 '0-UND self-contained' purity but now achieved through the ar-extract+ELF-reader path (proving the machinery end-to-end). (3b-WALL, named next round) general programs whose closure reaches the sanctioned libc leaves keep those UNDs; to RUN binutils-free those leaves must be closed either by the ongoing raw-svc leaf-porting campaign (write/getpid/setpgid already syscall-routed; alloc_syscall_native.o is the mmap-arena malloc) or by extending the same reader/fixpoint to also extract a static libc.a. That libc-floor closure is explicitly the round-4 target, not this round. Verdict: gate round-3 GREEN on (3a) a libc-free minimal exec (nm-UND ∅, exit-code verified) + a byteeq-neutral proof that the loop edit doesn't perturb round-1/2; declare the sanctioned-floor libc UND as the measured wall for round-4.
test_plan: MINIMAL END-TO-END (pool, linux x86_64): author a round-3 test program whose main returns a value computed by ONE runtime call, exit-code-verified (no print/malloc/write, keeping the closure smallest + libc-free) — e.g. `fn main() -> int { return hexa_add(40, 2) }` so the payload -> own-start `mov edi,edx` -> exit(42). Build own .o via `--backend=native --emit=exec --linker=hexa target=x86_64-linux-gnu`; the program has an UNDEF `hexa_add`, so dispatch hits link_elf_x86_64_ownstart_ar with HEXA_PREBUILT_RUNTIME=<pool runtime.a>. Verify: (1) the exec runs with ZERO binutils/clang/ld/as and `echo $?` == 42; (2) `nm -u <exec>` == ∅ (proves 3a self-contained libc-free closure — if it shows libc leaves, that's the 3b wall -> pick an even smaller pure symbol or record the wall). Choose the test symbol by first dumping, on the pool, the transitive member+UND closure of a few candidate leaf runtime fns and picking the one with fewest members and no libc UND. UNIT-TEST THE ELF .o READER IN ISOLATION (pure darwin/mini, no clang/ld/pool — mirrors compiler/test/elf_x86_64_data.hexa idiom): build an ElfX86Obj by hand (or via pack_lir_x86_64 of a small hand LModule), `serialize_elf_x86_64(obj)` -> write_bytes -> read_file_bytes -> `parse_elf_x86_obj` -> ASSERT round-trip equality: obj.text bytes, each ElfSym (name-string, normalized section slot, rebased value, bind/type), each ElfRel (offset, kind, addend, resolved sym name). Because serialize is the exact inverse the reader parses, this is a hermetic self-check that makes the reader NOT all-or-nothing. UNIT-TEST parse_ar_archive on hand-built GNU-ar bytes: construct '!<arch>\\n' + two 60-byte member headers (incl. a '//' long-name entry + a '/'+decimal indirect name) wrapping two serialize_elf_x86_64 blobs, assert member names/offsets/sizes + even-padding. UNIT-TEST archive_extract_fixpoint: wrap two synthetic ElfX86Objs (A defines f + UNDs g; B defines g) as a 2-member GNU-ar byte array, seed live-UND={f}, assert BOTH A and B pulled (transitive) and a member defining an unreferenced symbol is NOT pulled.
staged_order: Stage 1 — parse_elf_x86_obj + local _er_* byte helpers + section-index normalization. Independently verified by the pure-darwin serialize_elf_x86_64 -> read_file_bytes -> parse round-trip unit test (no clang/pool). This is the highest-risk/highest-reuse piece; land + prove it first so it is not entangled with ar/linker work.
Stage 2 — ArMember struct + parse_ar_archive. Verified independently on hand-built GNU-ar bytes (magic, 60-byte headers, '//' long-name table, '/'+decimal indirect, even-pad) on darwin.

Stage 3 — archive_extract_fixpoint. Verified with a synthetic 2-member GNU-ar byte array built from two Stage-1 serialized objs; assert transitive pull + non-pull of unreferenced members. Depends on 1+2 but testable without the linker or the pool.

Stage 4 — integration: extend link_elf_x86_64_ownstart data-segment reloc patch (prove byte-neutral for round-1/2 via byteeq 3-target) + new link_elf_x86_64_ownstart_ar wrapper + main.hexa dispatch + runtime.a discovery. Verified end-to-end on the pool: minimal own .o + real linux runtime.a -> running ET_EXEC exit(42), nm-UND ∅, zero binutils. This is the only stage needing the pool; stages 1-3 are hermetic darwin unit tests, so the round is NOT one untestable big-bang.
